output.title: Expected Wait Time for a Member Callback
output.draft_text:
Q: How long does a member usually wait for a callback?

A: After a callback is requested, a member can typically expect to hear back within [standard callback timeframe, e.g., number of business hours or business days]. Callbacks are made during [callback hours of operation and time zone].

Timeframes may differ depending on [factors affecting callback time, e.g., request type, department handling the request, urgent vs. non-urgent status, call volume]. For [urgent or time-sensitive request types], the expected callback time is [urgent callback timeframe].

When setting expectations with the member:
- Confirm the best phone number and preferred time to reach them.
- Tell them the expected callback window: [standard callback timeframe].
- Let them know how many attempts will be made: [number of callback attempts] and whether a voicemail will be left: [voicemail practice].

If the member has not received a callback within [escalation threshold timeframe], advise them to [next step, e.g., call back at the main number / ask for a supervisor / reference their case number], or escalate through [escalation path or team].

If the member's issue involves a deadline (for example, [examples of deadline-sensitive issues]), [instruction for handling deadline-sensitive callbacks].
placeholders: [standard callback timeframe, e.g., number of business hours or business days]
[callback hours of operation and time zone]
[factors affecting callback time, e.g., request type, department handling the request, urgent vs. non-urgent status, call volume]
[next step, e.g., call back at the main number / ask for a supervisor / reference their case number]
author_checklist: Confirm the official standard callback timeframe, and whether it is measured in business hours, business days, or calendar days.
Confirm the callback hours of operation and the time zone used.
Confirm whether callback timeframes differ by request type, department, or urgency, and list any such differences.
Confirm whether an expedited or urgent callback timeframe exists and which request types qualify.
Confirm how many callback attempts are made and whether voicemails are left, including any privacy restrictions on voicemail content.
Confirm the escalation threshold and the correct escalation path if a callback is missed.
Confirm how deadline-sensitive issues should be handled while a member waits for a callback.
Verify that any stated timeframes match contractual, regulatory, or service-level commitments, and that they are not presented as guarantees unless they are guaranteed.
Determine the correct knowledge base for this unit, since it may apply to member services broadly rather than only to benefits, and identify the owning team.
Remove any sections or placeholders that do not apply before approval.
